verdict: HOLD — the only broker in the cluster to beat inflation in every one of the last four and six years, at 71.00x earnings, 9.68x book and zero cash conversion
points: Not held — CHOICEIN is on your watchlist. Choice International, ₹16,186cr, retail broking and wealth management with an attached NBFC, investment bank, AMC and government-advisory arm — at ₹16,186cr the second-largest of the 14 capital-markets names re-peered out of bfsi_nbfc on 2026-10-22, behind CRISIL at ₹33,243cr. Re-peered out of bfsi_nbfc into bfsi_broker on 2026-10-22, so the percentiles below rank it against 42 broking and securities-dealing peers rather than against lenders. Quality 59, valuation 19, momentum 57, composite 32.

Its compounding record is the best in the cluster and the re-peering makes that claim stronger, not weaker. np_growth_above_inflation_5y 1.000 and _7y 1.000 are each first of the 32 brokers carrying the tests — net profit beat inflation in 4 of the last 4 year-steps and 6 of 6, the denominators being N-1 because each step needs two points — and _10y 0.889 is 8 of 9, second of 32. It shares the 5y and 7y top spot with SBI Funds Management, which is an asset manager misfiled into this cluster by the same kind of industry-label defect that put the capital-markets names in with the lenders, so among actual brokers it is alone. np_cagr_5y 41.97% is fourth of 33. v1 could only say this was the best of a hand-picked 16; it is the best of 32 peers.

The trailing year holds up, which is what separates it from the rest of the re-peered group. TTM sales +26.47%, operating profit +33.72%, net profit +32.48%, with opm_now 35.28% against opm_prev 33.37% — a +1.91pp step. Twelve of those 14 rows carry a margin-step or earnings-quality blocker of some kind — CHOICEIN's own is a cash-conversion flag rather than a margin break — so a business whose margin barely moved while profit grew a third is the most informative single fact here. roe_3y 16.33% and roce_3y 17.65% are both 16th of 43 — unremarkable, and earned without the balance-sheet distortion the old scorecard was reading.

Everything good about it has been paid for, and the cash is not arriving. pe_ttm 71.00x is the second-highest of the 37 brokers with a PE, behind only AVONMORE's 95.58x, and pb 9.68x is fifth of 43. There is no own-history anchor: its ten-year band low of 1.82x cannot be told apart from a split adjustment, so there is no way to say whether 71x is high or normal for this stock. Against that, cfo_pat_3y 0.000 puts it in the bottom nine of 42, all nine tied at the floor, and cash conversion was -0.64 in FY2026 — three years in which operating cash did not arrive at all, in a business with a lending arm that consumes it. fii_pct 10.10% is fifth of 36 and the close held above its 200-day EMA on 63.10% of the last 252 sessions, fourth of 32. tech_net_score_scaled is NULL for every scored company on the platform; the momentum pillar renormalises around the components that do exist, so the percentile is a narrower question than the scorecard asks rather than a lost weight.

The uncomfortable part: the best compounding record of 32 brokers belongs to the second-most-expensive one, whose three-year cash conversion is zero. A perfect 4-of-4 and 6-of-6 inflation record deserves a premium — but 71.00x earnings and 9.68x book on retail broking means two years of lower market turnover takes a third off the earnings and the multiple at once, and a business that reports profit without collecting it has no cushion when that happens. Hold if you own it. Adding at 71x requires believing Indian retail participation only goes one way, which is the assumption this entire cluster is built on and which none of its 43 members has been tested through a bear market.
trigger_text: cfo_pat_3y turning positive while opm_now holds near 35% -> the profit is real cash, the inflation record is structural, and 71.00x is a growth multiple rather than a cycle multiple. Market turnover falling with opm_now under 28%, or cash conversion staying negative -> a 9.68x book on broking revenue de-rates far faster than the earnings fall, which is how every broker in this cluster has previously broken.

verdict: WATCH — worst of all 16 wealth names on four separate measures at once, composite down 61 to 15, with the price still above its 200-day EMA on three-quarters of the year
points: Not held — PRIMESECU is on your watchlist. Prime Securities, ₹952cr, investment banking, corporate advisory and wealth management. Its own maturity bucket is under the 10-peer floor, so this row mixes tiers to reach a usable pool. Quality 27, valuation 55, momentum 41, composite 15 — the lowest of the 14 capital-markets names re-peered out of bfsi_nbfc on 2026-10-22, and down from 61 before the re-peering.

It is the worst row in its pool on four measures, and they are the four that matter. opm_now 10.22% is the lowest of all 16, ttm_np_pct -87.29% the lowest, ttm_op_pct -72.08% the lowest, and np_yoy_q -80.82% the lowest. Not bottom-quartile — last, four times. opm_now 10.22% against opm_prev 41.85% is a -31.63pp step, the largest single-year margin break of the 14 re-peered names and the pack's first blocker here. The quarter confirms the year rather than softening it, and cash conversion was -0.10 in FY2026 against a prior mean of +0.23. There is no pe_ttm at all: the earnings base has effectively gone, so the valuation pillar scored on 45% of its declared weight.

The long record is genuinely respectable, which is the whole tension. roe_avg_above_threshold_10y 0.500 — five of ten years above the hurdle — is fourth of the nine names with the test, and np_consistency_10y 1.657 is sixth of nine. That is a middling-to-decent decade, not a chronic underperformer. An advisory firm with that history and one catastrophic year is a different proposition from one that was always marginal, and the re-peering sharpened this rather than changing it: against asset and wealth managers the decade reads ordinary where against lenders it read strong.

But the price is behaving as though nothing happened. The close held above its 200-day EMA on 74.21% of the last 252 sessions — fifth of the 11 with the reading — and ret_12m_rel +2.80% is positive and sixth of 12. The stock is near its highs while operating profit fell 72% and the margin fell 32 points. Its own ten-year PE band of 7.00-59.23x averaging 21.04x is quotable and cannot be applied: there is no current E to compare it to. tech_net_score_scaled is NULL for every scored company on the platform; the momentum pillar renormalises around the components that do exist, so the percentile is a narrower question than the scorecard asks rather than a lost weight.

The uncomfortable answer first: this is the one row in the batch where the market's price and the company's accounts are telling opposite stories, and no number in the pack resolves which is right. A deal-driven advisory book can lose 87% of its profit to mandate timing and get it back in one transaction — or the fee pipeline is gone and the price has not found out. Watch rather than act, because a position taken now is a bet on which of those it is, taken at no discount whatsoever. Look at the next quarter's revenue line, not its profit line. The composite falling 61 to 15 on re-peering is not new information about the company; it is the old number having been flattering.
trigger_text: opm_now recovering above 30% with np_yoy_q turning positive -> the collapse was mandate timing, the five-of-ten hurdle decade is the real business, and the price was right to ignore it. A second quarter near 10% margins while the close stays above its 200-day EMA -> the gap between accounts and price closes downward, and 74.21% above-EMA becomes the risk rather than the comfort.
